RetailMax Inc. - Q4 FY2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the RetailMax Inc. Q4 FY2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RetailMax Inc.'s results for the Q4 FY2023. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer; and Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report RetailMax Inc.'s performance for the Q4 FY2023. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We posted total revenue of $4.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year, with gross margins expanding 85 basis points to 38.2%, reflecting our pricing discipline and mix shift to higher-margin private labels.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital sales accelerated 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, now 32% of total sales, outpacing the industry thanks to our omnichannel fulfillment advantages.

3. Store Performance: Our remodel program drove 16.5% comps growth in upgraded locations, well ahead of the company average of 4.2%, enhancing productivity and customer dwell time.

4. Marketing Initiatives: Omnichannel sales like BOPIS and curbside hit $285 million, up 28%, representing 22% of digital sales and lifting overall margins through low-cost store fulfillment.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Inventory turnover reached 5.6x for the full year and 6.8x in Q4, ahead of peers, with days inventory on hand down to 65 from 76 year-over-year.

6. Loyalty Program Update: Advanced inventory strategies, including AI forecasting and vendor collaboration, freed up $450 million in working capital while cutting stockouts 28%.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q4 FY2023.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $4.2 billion, an 8% increase compared to the same period last year, propelled by 4.2% same-store sales growth, e-commerce acceleration, and contributions from 15 net new stores in high-growth Sunbelt markets.

Gross margin was 38.2%, expanding 85 basis points year-over-year. This marks our third straight quarter of expansion and lifts the trailing four-quarter average to 38%. The outperformance versus our initial guidance stems from our stores-first approach, capitalizing on traffic recovery and tight inventory controls for better mix and pricing leverage. Merchandise margins, the heart of gross profit, rose 92 basis points to around 40%, mainly from a 2.3-point shift toward stronger categories. Apparel and home goods, now 42% of sales, rose 8% year-over-year on exclusive private labels such as Haven Home Essentials and Urban Thread, which offer over 1,000 basis points more margin than national brands. These are sourced via expanded partnerships in Southeast Asia and U.S. mills, hitting 48% margins against 35% for direct vendor items. Hardlines like patio and outdoor products also gained from stabilized supply chains after earlier Red Sea issues. Pricing held firm, with average unit retail up 1.8% despite softer discretionary demand. Our AI dynamic pricing across 85% of our 1,200 stores fine-tuned everyday low prices on 15,000 SKUs, trimming promo depth by 20 basis points while supporting 2.1% comps. This echoes successful models at peers like TJX. On costs, COGS dipped 7 basis points as a share of sales, with ocean freight falling from $12,000 per FEU peak to $3,200, saving $45 million sequentially. Vendor deals locked multi-year terms on private-label cotton blends, countering 2.5% inflation from El Niño. Shrink improved 25 basis points to 1.4%, best in five years, via Eagle Eye RFID in 70% of stores cutting organized crime 18% and Zebra exit analytics tackling urban theft—key as industry shrink rose 32% per NRF. Regionally, Northeast and Midwest—65% of space—gained 110 basis points on 4.2% traffic from back-to-school and holidays. Sunbelt added 65 basis points via remodel beauty bays. Canada felt 20 basis points drag from CAD strength and lumber, offset by 28% private-label sales penetration. Occupancy eased 7 basis points to 8.9% on comps and nine closures versus seven greenfields. Distribution efficiencies added 12 basis points with Ohio and Nevada DC automation trimming inbound costs 11%. Our model thrives with 55% BOPIS driving full-price sales and markdowns down 30 basis points to 9.2%. For Q1 FY2024, we see another 60-90 basis points expansion on holiday gift mix, freight relief, and GenAI shrink prediction.

Operating expenses were $1.2 billion, representing 28.5% of revenue, reflecting disciplined cost management amid wage pressures and marketing investments.

Net income was $320 million, or $1.55 per share.

We generated $450 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently $1.2 billion, down 8% from last year's Q4 peak.

Delving deeper into inventory, our turnover ratio—a vital metric for brick-and-mortar operators—measures COGS divided by average inventory, showing how effectively we refresh stock amid apparel trends, holiday hardlines, and fast-moving consumables. A solid annual rate above 5x keeps margins intact and markdowns low; slow turns tie up cash in obsolescence, fast ones risk Black Friday stockouts. For FY2023, we hit 5.6x, up 17% from 4.8x in FY2022, surpassing Macy's 4.2x and Kohl's 5.1x. Q4 reached 6.8x, strongest in five years, on 4.2% holiday comps. Average inventory fell 8% despite 12% COGS growth to $8.1 billion from private-label volume. By category, apparel/softlines led at 7.2x from 6.1x via 4-6 week micro-cycles on athleisure partnerships. Hardlines hit 5.4x from 4.7x on evergreen items like pod coffee makers and vacuums. Footwear at 4.9x faced sneaker softness but promotions help. This cut DIOH to 65 days from 76, below NRF's 85-day department store norm. Regionally, Southeast topped 7.1x on tourism and 15 Sunbelt openings; Midwest 5.8x on grilling; Northeast 4.9x hit by storms curbing Boston/Philly traffic 2-3%; West Coast 5.7x aided by 28% BOPIS digital sales. Drivers included DC optimization with Manhattan Associates AI demand sensing boosting forecast accuracy 22%, trimming safety stock 15% sans stockouts; supplier scorecards for P&G/Levi's VMI on 40% SKUs to weekly replen; dynamic pricing cutting clearance to 3% from 5.5%, holding margins at 38.2%. Our Efficient Assortment 2.0 uses stores as micro-fulfillment hubs, with ship-from-store at 35% e-com. FY2024 guide: 5.8x-6.2x, risks from tariffs adding 50 bps DIOH or port issues, mitigated by Mexico nearshoring 20% hardlines; upside from RFID in 200 stores tagging 70% high-value SKUs for cycle counts and 1.2% shrink.

Complementing this, our strategies for inventory optimization are central to profitability against Amazon and Wayfair, tackling disruptions, tariffs, and value shifts. In Q4, turnover rose to 5.8x from 4.2x, beating 5.5x target, dropping DIO to 63 days from 87, unlocking $450 million working capital or 15% of end inventory. Stockouts fell 28% to 3.2%, overstock 22% to 12%, adding 120 bps to 38.2% merchandise margins and 142% GMROI above NRF 110%. Four pillars: advanced forecasting with Blue Yonder on Oracle Retail, incorporating 50 signals like Conference Board confidence, IBM weather, events, TikTok sentiment—predicting 15% activewear lift in Sunbelt for 7-day cycles, cutting stockouts 35%; Northeast cut outerwear 18% for fleece pivot; Southeast adjusted rain gear 25%. Accuracy hit 92% store-SKU, down excess 9%. Omnichannel: ship-from-store 18% e-com from 9%, BOPIS/curbside 32% digital; RFID 85% apparel/footwear for 2-hour urban fulfillment. Home goods grilling allocated 20% in-store to online, up sell-through 41%, margins +250 bps. SKU pruning: cut 18% or 4,500 low-sell-through items like Shein-style fashion for private basics at 55% margins. Vendor VMI 35% CPG with P&G penalties, down safety stock 25% or $120M at 98% in-stock. Store tech: AMRs in 150 stores cut fulfillment labor 22%, same-day BOPIS; AI vision shrink to 1.1%. FY2025 target 6.5x, DIO<55, RFID 95%, blockchain organics. Sunbelt 40 new stores offset Midwest closures vs. Walmart pressure.

Shifting to e-commerce sales growth year-over-year, it remains key to our omnichannel edge amid moderating spending and inflation. E-commerce rose 28% to $1.2 billion in Q4, 32% of net sales from 26% last year—11th straight double-digit quarter, topping U.S. retail e-comm's 8% per Census. Traffic up 22%, mobile app 62% sessions via AR try-on and 3D planners, app conversion 4.2x web. AOV +5% to $145 on Adobe Sensei upsell +18%; conversions 3.8% from 3.1% with one-click pay, abandonment -24%. Apparel 42% digital up 32% on TikTok/Instagram $150M GMV; home/furniture 41% on West Elm exclusives; electronics 15% offset by bundles. U.S. 31% to $1.02B, high Sunbelt penetration; int'l UK/Canada 19% to $180M pre-Europe ramp. Headless AWS/Fastly: 99.99% uptime, <1.5s loads. Dynamic pricing on store inventory; ship-from-store 45% orders <2 days 78%; BOPIS/curbside +55% to $450M, BOPIS users spend 25% more. Fulfillment 12.5% flat, vs. peers' headwinds; e-comm margins 38.2%. FY2024 25-27%, $250M capex robotics/blockchain; 28% private-label. Rewards 45M members 65% repeat moat.

Our omnichannel initiatives like BOPIS and curbside under ReadyRightNow are transforming experiences versus Amazon's 38% e-comm GMV. Q4 omnichannel $285M, +28% YoY, 22% digital from 17%—10th 25%+ quarter. BOPIS 62% or 1.2M txns +32%; curbside 18% or 450K +24%. +150 bps margin lift, store costs 4-6% vs. 12-15% parcel. 68% BOPIS add items, ticket $145 +18%; apparel 28% digital; curbside repeats 4.2x. OMS/Manhattan RFID 85% stores, out-of-stock -40% to 2%, 96% <30min; app Scan&Reserve +22%; IoT beacons 600 lots, waits 4.2min, NPS 82. Southeast 35% growth 320 stores; Northeast 26%; Midwest 19% rural fix 50 pop-ups; West 8% DoorDash pilots +15%. De-risks vs. e-slowdown, digital +14% vs. Amazon 10%; 12% $150B omni share, traffic +11%, 2.5x $45M capex ROI. Q1 25-30%, BOPIS+ styling, curbside 95%, drone rural. 55% Rewards omni +12 pts, 4-6% FY2025 comps.

On store remodel and renovation plans, it's high-ROI for comps, productivity, omni blend. FY2023 120 remodels at $1.8M/store or $45/sqft 40K prototype, 28% ROI 24 months, +150 bps margins. FY2024 $350M capex 40% total $875M for 180 remodels, 220 FY2025, $120M next-gen AI/sustain, $650M rev 22-mo payback $450M NPV. McKinsey/RetailFlow data: open layouts +20% discovery, dwell +18% conv +12% basket +$4.50 to $52; 15-20 kiosks ShopGenius AR try-on -22% returns, mobile POS BOPIS 28% sales; LED/HVAC -25% energy $15M rebates, 60% recycled fixtures GenZ appeal; RFGen3 RFID 85% SKUs -40bps shrink; Swisslog backroom -35% pick. Southeast 65 stores 22% comps Atlanta Hispanic lines; Northeast 45 urban 15K sqft $650/spsf; Midwest/West 70 +16% conv EV chargers. Remodeled 16.5% comps vs. 4.2%, EBITDA +220bps 12.8%, turns 5.8x. Retailtainment 35% growth per McKinsey, Rewards +25% enrollment. Outpaces Macy's, matches Best Buy. Risks delays/vendor diversif. 5-7% comps, +100bps margins.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Ramirez, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to Emily Patel to discuss store operations.

David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our sustainable apparel line in partnership with eco-focused brands, which has seen exceptional demand with sell-through rates exceeding 75% in the first 30 days. Early feedback highlights strong appeal in athleisure and home essentials, aligning with our private-label push, and we are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches like expanded organic groceries.

Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented enhanced omnichannel pickup zones and micro-fulfillment in 150 locations, and are seeing positive results with BOPIS conversion up 32% and overall store traffic from digital orders rising 11%.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has been a headwind, but our pricing discipline—up 1.8% on average unit retail—and dynamic AI tools across 85% of stores allowed us to reduce promotional depth while holding 2.1% comps. The shift to 42% sales in high-margin apparel and home private labels added over 92 basis points to merchandise margins, helping us expand overall gross margin to 38.2%. We're passing through normalized freight savings and vendor concessions effectively.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Maria. For Q1 FY2024, we expect same-store sales growth of 4% to 6%, incorporating holiday momentum, remodel lifts averaging 16.5% in upgraded stores, and 25-30% omnichannel growth. This assumes stable spending, with upside from Sunbelt traffic and BOPIS+ rollout, offset by any Northeast weather risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Alex. We've boosted forecast accuracy 22% with AI demand sensing across 50 external signals, enabling 15% safety stock cuts without stockouts over 2%. Vendor-managed inventory covers 40% SKUs with weekly cadences and penalties, while Manhattan WMS in six DCs and RFID pilots reduce shrink. Nearshoring 20% hardlines to Mexico counters port and tariff risks, driving our 5.6x FY turnover.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Green with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Green (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Rachel. Our Family Rewards program, with 45 million members, drives 65% repeat rates and now 55% omnichannel penetration among top tiers, up 12 points. Members using BOPIS spend 25% more annually, with 68% adding in-store items for higher tickets. It's fueling traffic up 11% from pickups and supports our 4-6% comp guide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera (Citigroup):
Thanks. On inventory turnover, how sustainable is the 5.6x, and any category risks?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Tom, the 5.6x is sustainable via Efficient Assortment 2.0, with apparel at 7.2x on micro-cycles and hardlines 5.4x on evergreens. Footwear's 4.9x is promotional focus; FY2024 guide 5.8x-6.2x. RFID expansion to 70% high-value SKUs and SKU pruning keep DIOH low.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the Q&A portion. I'll now turn it back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
